lines.text: Do you know NASA crashed one of its best spacecraft into Saturn, on purpose?
This is Cassini, built from NASA's own 3D model. It studied Saturn for thirteen years.
It found something amazing. Enceladus, a small icy moon, sprays water into space, from an ocean under its ice.
An ocean could mean life. And Cassini was running low on fuel. Left to drift, it could one day hit a moon like that, and bring germs from Earth.
So for its grand finale, Cassini dove between Saturn and its rings, twenty-two times. No spacecraft had ever done that.
Then, on September fifteenth, twenty seventeen, it flew straight into Saturn, sending data until the very end.
Its last signal took eighty-three minutes to reach Earth. By then, Cassini was already gone.
Sometimes the right thing is to make sure something is gone. Orbi Transfer lets you do that too.
Destroy a file you sent, and it's gone for everyone, right away. Only the sender can do it.
